DNRPA registry: new passenger-car body types (~EU M1) of every brand. Records carry no fuel field - powertrain classified from the model name and checked against ACARA's electrified totals; MHEV is a lower bound; no petrol/diesel split.
DNRPA registry: Whole where the first owner is a natural person (persona física). Private + Industry = Whole. Powertrain classified from the model name.
DNRPA registry: Whole where the first owner is a legal person (companies / state / fleets). Private + Industry = Whole. Powertrain classified from the model name.
New passenger cars (M1). One combined hybrid figure: shown as 'Hybrid', counted within ICE, no PHEV curve. Dec-2025 BEV spike: VAT exemption for EV imports ended 2026-01-01.
MIA vehicle register: Whole where the owner is a natural person (PERSON = P). Private + Industry = Whole. Combined hybrid bucket, no PHEV split.
MIA vehicle register: Whole where the owner is a legal person (companies, state, fleets; PERSON = J). Private + Industry = Whole. Combined hybrid bucket, no PHEV split.
Used imports at their first Ukrainian registration - not new cars; customs-policy changes move it in steps. One combined hybrid figure.
MIA vehicle register: new goods vehicles with a gross vehicle weight up to 3,500 kg (EU N1), by the register's new-vehicle operation codes.
New private cars (EU M1); full and mild hybrids counted in petrol. EV tax concession cut Apr 2024 and ended Apr 2026: spikes before each, BEV share steps down after.
Used imports (mostly Japanese-market MPVs) - not new cars. Hybrids counted in petrol.
New light goods vehicles up to 3.5 t (EU N1); Hong Kong's heavier LGVs (to 5.5 t) excluded. Low volume.
Domestic sales of all vehicle types incl. commercial - not M1 registrations. Tesla missing before 2024, so BEV is understated up to 2023. Imported hybrids include mild hybrids.
New cars and SUVs (EU M1), may incl. near-new used imports (max. 2 model years); pickups are in Peru (Vans). HEV incl. mild hybrids. No data for April 2020 (COVID-19).

SUNARP first registrations (via AAP BI-AAP): pickups, chassis-cabs, dropside and box vans, and panel vans (EU N1), from 2019-01; may include near-new used imports. Diesel-dominated; plug-ins are a handful a month (JAC T8 EV, BYD Shark).
Customs imports of new cars, not registrations - single months can run ahead of sales. Pickups not included. HEV includes mild hybrids.
New cars and SUVs (EU M1); pickups and vans are in Ecuador (Vans). Plug-ins identified by model. HEV includes mild hybrids and Nissan e-POWER.
Pickups (most of it), panel vans and van-based minibuses (about EU N1; some passenger minivans included).
New passenger cars up to 9 seats, from 2021. HEV includes Nissan e-POWER. Monthly BEV swings with Tesla's quarter-end deliveries - read the trend.
New goods vehicles up to 3.5 t (about EU N1); since Sep 2020 also 3.5-5 t vehicles up to 6 m long.

THB register (MOTC statistics): new goods vehicles over 3.5 t ('large goods vehicle' ≈ EU N2+N3, tractor units included), from 2021-01 — since 2020-09-04 without the 3.5–5 t vehicles up to 6 m long (now in Vans). Almost entirely diesel.
New buses and coaches (EU M2+M3). Small and lumpy (100-200 a month); the BEV share follows the city-bus electrification programme.
Mild hybrids are inside petrol/diesel. March and September (plate changes) carry about a quarter of the year each - compare a month with the same month a year earlier.
Whole new-vehicle market (cars, bakkies, trucks, buses) - not M1. Quarterly. More brands report from 2026, which lifts NEV counts a little.

New passenger-car SALES (≈ M1, not registrations): VAMA members + VAMA's estimate of non-member imports + VinFast deliveries + Hyundai (TC Group). Non-member imports (no fuel split) shown as Other; Hyundai as ICE; no PHEV split. Hybrids in ICE before 2024; VinFast for 2022-09/10 and 2023-08 to 2024-08 is a year figure spread evenly (Yearly points).
